title: Celestis Health escalation - postmortem follow-up
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-07-16
Time: 14:00 - 14:54 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Record: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Evan Liu (Redwood CSM), Marta Gomez (Celestis VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Celestis SRE), Ravi Patel (Celestis CISO)
summary: Follow-up on the July 8th production incident where Celestis observed elevated p95 latency and user-facing 5xx errors. Discussed root cause (autoscaler misconfiguration leading to KV cache thrashing and fallback model variants), short-term mitigations, long-term reliability improvements, security/docs requests, and agreed next steps including benchmarks and an updated autoscaling policy. Redwood to deliver configuration patch, incident timeline, and run a joint load replay test next week.
topics: Root cause: autoscaler + KV cache eviction
Long-term reliability improvements: warmup, canaries, better health checks
action_items: Priya Desai - share proposed autoscaler tweak (minNodes, scaleWindow) and example helm values - due 2026-07-20
Jordan Meyers - send incident timeline + raw request logs we can share (redacted) - due 2026-07-18
Liam O'Connor - provide sample traffic profile for load replay (QPS, common seq lengths) - due 2026-07-19
Evan Liu - schedule joint load replay with Celestis and Redwood infra team - due 2026-07-22
Ravi Patel - confirm list of required security docs (SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration checklist) - due 2026-07-21
next_steps: Redwood to publish autoscaler patch and canary playbook
Run a joint load replay on 2026-07-23 (target: full traffic spike for 30m)
Redwood to provide step-by-step rollback docs and emergency runbooks
Celestis to validate KMS/HSM integration details with Redwood security team
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, I'll kick us off, we've got about 55 minutes on the calendar, goal here is to walk through the postmortem actions from the July 8th outage and make sure owners and timelines are clear.
[00:00:12] Marta: thanks Jordan, appreciate it, this has been high priority for us, customers were impacted, so want to make progress.
[00:00:20] Priya: quick apologies, audio is a bit crackly for me, i'll chime in on the infra stuff, i pulled together the draft autoscaler changes.
[00:00:30] Liam: yeah thanks, i'll note as we go, i was on-call that night, saw the p95 spike at 02:14 and then the 5xx burst.
[00:00:38] Jordan: okay can we do a quick blast of the timeline, Priya you had the root cause summary?
[00:00:44] Priya: yeah, so tl;dr we saw an autoscaling policy that was too aggressive on scale-to-zero-ish behavior and combined with large sequence length variance in Celestis requests we got KV cache evictions. that caused a lot of cold starts and fallback to smaller model variants, which increased token generation latency and then triggered request timeouts upstream. also the health check we had for the model worker didn't detect degraded kv-warm state, so autoscaler removed nodes thinking they were idle.
[00:01:12] Marta: i remember seeing the logs where KV cache was being constantly rebuilt, some of the lines are garbled in our dashboard, but yes that matches.
[00:01:20] Ravi: can you clarify "KV cache" — is that the redwood kv cache or something on our side? i want to make sure we have the right ownership for encryption at rest.
[00:01:28] Priya: good q, it's in the Redwood serving runtime, it's the prefix/KV cache that keeps key-value pairs for decoder state across requests. Redwood manages it in the hosted cluster, but config controls (like cache TTL and warmup) are surfaceable.
[00:01:45] Ravi: ok so for encryption, does that sit behind our KMS or yours?
[00:01:50] Jordan: short answer: for hosted the KV content is ephemeral and encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed keys by default; for private/dedicated we can hook into customer KMS. we'll follow up with security docs.
[00:01:59] Liam: the crash sequence for us — we hit a traffic spike, autoscaler started terminating nodes because the CPU was low, but because KV warm state wasn't present the p95 latency jumped from 180ms to 2.5s within a few minutes. retries piled up and overloaded the ingress.
[00:02:19] Marta: i think one of the misconfig items on our side was the client timeout being too short, so the frontend retried quickly which amplified load.
[00:02:25] Jordan: that makes sense, we should treat retry policies as part of the mitigation playbook.
[00:02:30] Priya: immediate mitigation we applied was to raise the min replica count and extend the cooldown window for the autoscaler, also disabled aggressive bin-packing so nodes don't get preemptively removed. that dropped the error rate back to baseline.
[00:02:44] Liam: and we rolled back the last deploy as well because there was a model change flagged that night, not sure it was causal but we wanted to reduce variables.
[00:02:52] Marta: was that rollback the Redwood side or our deployment?
[00:02:56] Priya: rollback on the serving config we pushed via the Dedicated control plane, so Redwood reverted the model variant routing change.
[00:03:03] Jordan: there was also a gap in tracing — we didn't correlate KV eviction events to the autoscaler events in the same timeline, so we took longer to identify root cause. we'll include improved tracing tags in the patch.
[00:03:15] Ravi: from security perspective we need preserved audit logs for that period; can you confirm retention and what you can provide?
[00:03:22] Evan: yes we'll export the audit trail for 2026-07-08 01:30-03:30 UTC, redacted for PII, and share S3 link to the logs.
[00:03:30] Marta: perfect. next, long-term fixes?
[00:03:33] Priya: long-term we recommend three things — (1) autoscaler policy tuning (min nodes, scale window, health check improvements), (2) warmup/wedge behavior for KV cache on node start (pre-populate from persistent store for common prefixes), and (3) better canarying and model-variant fallback policies with circuit-breakers to avoid cascading retries.
[00:03:54] Liam: can you expand on the warmup? what does that add in terms of latency on start?
[00:04:00] Priya: warmup will add a small startup cost but drastically reduce early p95. basically when a node is added we run a warmup job that primes the KV store with recent prefixes (based on a rolling window) so first user requests hit hot cache. we think 30-60 seconds of warmup per node is enough for typical usage.
[00:04:18] Marta: i'm worried about cost impact with less aggressive scaling. can we find a balance?
[00:04:23] Jordan: totally, the optimize team has metrics to show marginal cost vs p95 improvements. we'll run a cost simulation for your traffic profile and propose target thresholds (e.g., keep a small buffer of warm nodes during predictable spike windows).
[00:04:36] Ravi: regarding encryption and KMS — if we move to dedicated or private, what's the path to use our KMS?
[00:04:42] Priya: we have an integration path for both dedicated and private where customer KMS keys are used for data at rest. we'll share the KMS integration checklist and an example of how keys are rotated.
[00:04:52] Jordan: ok action items — Priya will draft autoscaler values and the canary playbook, Jordan will send timeline and logs, Evan will coordinate the joint load replay, Liam will provide traffic profile and Ravi will confirm security doc list.
[00:05:05] Marta: do we have an ETA on the autoscaler patch?
[00:05:08] Priya: we can get a first-draft config out by Monday the 20th, and a minor patch we can roll into your staging cluster by Wed the 22nd.
[00:05:16] Liam: once it's in staging i'd like to run a 30-minute spike test with realistic seq length distribution.
[00:05:21] Priya: yep we'll do that, also include a scenario where we replay sudden cold-starts to validate warmup.
[00:05:28] Marta: any SLA credits or remediation options? legal is asking.
[00:05:32] Jordan: we can open a formal support credit request and engage the account team; we'll put a note to support and include the incident cause in the request. i'll follow up with your procurement contact.
[00:05:41] Ravi: i still have one outstanding on audit and forensic data — do you keep the raw model logs or only ingress traces?
[00:05:48] Evan: we keep both traces and worker logs for 90 days by default, and longer with enterprise retention add-ons. we'll export the worker logs for the target window to the secure S3 link.
[00:05:58] Jordan: ok let's go deeper — Priya can you walk through the proposed autoscaler settings and why each param helps?
[00:06:05] Priya: sure, params: minReplicas=3 (prevents scale-to-zero), scaleWindow=180s (longer cooldown to avoid thrash), targetCPU=65% (so we preserve headroom), warmupGracePeriod=60s (delay eviction of KV within 60s of start). also healthProbe change to check kv-warm flag rather than just worker liveness.
[00:06:31] Liam: i like the kv-warm probe but how is that exposed? is it an endpoint on the agent?
[00:06:36] Priya: yes it's lightweight /health?kv_state which returns a primary/secondary with a confidence score. we can make it opt-in for a couple weeks.
[00:06:44] Marta: opt-in is fine, but we need the default to be safe.
[00:06:47] Jordan: noted. on the canary playbook — we also recommend an automatic rollback threshold tied to regenerated p95 and error rate with a half-life smoothing, so flapping won't cause noisy rollbacks.
[00:06:59] Priya: and we'll add tracing tags: autoscaler_event_id, kv_eviction_count, and model_variant_id to make postmortem correlation easier.
[00:07:09] Ravi: sounds good, what about audit attestation for SOC2? we need specific artifacts for the legal team.
[00:07:15] Evan: we'll assemble the SOC2-related artifacts: system architecture diagrams, access logs, key rotation history (masked), and the incident report summary.
[00:07:23] Marta: will you include the remediation timeline in the report?
[00:07:26] Evan: yes, we'll include a timeline, mitigations taken, long-term fixes planned, and owners.
[00:07:32] Jordan: ok let's capture the immediate things that would reduce blast radius if this happens again: increase minReplicas in prod to 3 during business hours, add retry jitter in the frontend to avoid retry storms, and add canary ramping at 10% increments over 20 minutes.
[00:07:49] Priya: also include an incident runbook snippet for SRE: how to detect kv thrash (metric: kv_eviction_rate > X per min), how to temporarily increase min replicas, and how to trigger a controlled rollback. we'll send that.
[00:08:02] Liam: on the replay test, i'll provide a capture of our peak hour traffic and the distribution of sequence lengths; can you simulate that in your staging?
[00:08:10] Priya: yes we have a replay harness, but need the exact hashed prefixes and QPS timeline from you to make it accurate.
[00:08:17] Marta: we'll export it, but note some data is sensitive, so if you need raw traces we'll have to sign an NDA addendum.
[00:08:24] Jordan: understood, we can accept redacted traces or hashed payloads. we'll only use it for the replay test and destroy after.
[00:08:30] Ravi: on the KMS front — i want a clear doc showing what keys are used for which artifacts so our compliance team can verify separation of duties.
[00:08:38] Evan: we'll include that in the security bundle.
[00:08:41] Marta: ok what's the schedule to close the loop? when should we meet again?
[00:08:45] Jordan: propose a checkpoint after the staging replay — target 2026-07-24, then a final sign-off after production patching one week later.
[00:08:53] Liam: fine by me.
[00:08:55] Priya: i'll push the autoscaler draft to the shared doc now and tag owners.
[00:08:59] Jordan: any other outstanding questions?
[00:09:02] Ravi: just one — in the future can Redwood provide a hot-fail fallback to a smaller context model without changing model_variant routing, i.e., keep latency bounded?
[00:09:12] Priya: we can implement a latency-based fallback that preserves context length but reduces beam size/temperature to keep latency under threshold; it's on the roadmap but we can prioritize for your account.
[00:09:24] Marta: thanks. if there's nothing else i think we're aligned on owners.
[00:09:29] Jordan: great, we'll follow up with the artifacts: autoscaler patch, incident timeline, worker logs, security bundle, and the replay schedule. thanks everyone.
[00:09:37] [crosstalk] brief wrap, people dropping off
[00:12:00] [00:12:00] (recording shows some cross-talk and brief pauses while documents were shared, meeting continues with smaller discussion about billing implications and support credit process)
[00:15:32] Evan: regarding credits, i'll open a support ticket with details and cc the account team, we can begin that flow parallel to the technical work.
[00:20:10] Jordan: note for internal, we should mark this as P1 follow-up and include the optimize team for cost sim.
[00:27:50] Priya: i'll also include an example helm/values yaml snippet in the doc, it's a one-liner to set minReplicas and the warmup flag.
[00:35:00] Liam: ok i'm going to drop off to catch a customer incident but will monitor the support ticket.
[00:43:12] Marta: thanks again, appreciate the quick response from Redwood on this.
[00:53:45] Jordan: all right closing notes: expect the draft configs + timeline in the next 48 hours, we'll reconvene after the staging replay.
[00:54:00] meeting end
final_notes: Owners and deadlines captured in action_items above. Redwood to provide redacted logs and autoscaler patch; Celestis to provide traffic profile and confirm security doc list. Plan: staging run 2026-07-23, check-in 2026-07-24.
legal_and_security_notes: Customer requested SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration checklist. Redwood to deliver security bundle and audit logs. Potential NDA addendum for raw traces if needed.
